snowflake.name: snowflake

account.name: account
account.title: Snowflake Account
account.desc: Top-level entry point for auditing a Snowflake account and every object it contains: `users`, `roles`, `databases`, `warehouses`, `stages`, `shares`, `apiIntegrations`, `tags`, `failoverGroups`, and account-level privileges via `grants`. The account-wide security posture is reachable through `securityIntegrations`, `passwordPolicies`, `networkPolicies`, `sessionPolicies`, `authenticationPolicies`, `maskingPolicies`, and `secrets`, while `resourceMonitors` exposes credit-usage guardrails for warehouses. `accountAdmins` lists the users that hold the ACCOUNTADMIN role, directly or through role grants, so you can review the account's most privileged identities.

alert.name: alert
alert.title: Snowflake alert
alert.desc: Alert in a schema, keyed by name, a scheduled check that evaluates a SQL condition and runs a SQL action whenever the condition returns rows. An alert runs on a schedule with the owner's rights and no caller, so `condition` and `action` together are the record of what it reads and what it does, which makes it both a monitoring control and an automation surface worth reviewing. A suspended alert stops running silently, so `state` shows whether a control that is configured is actually operating. Select an alert by name, for example `snowflake.account.alerts.where(state == "suspended")`.

apiIntegration.name: apiIntegration
apiIntegration.title: Snowflake API Integration
apiIntegration.desc: API integration object holding the cloud authentication context that external functions and Git repository integrations use to reach an HTTPS proxy service. The `type` field selects the backing provider (aws_api_gateway, azure_api_management, or google_api_gateway) and determines which credential fields carry a value. Auditing these matters because the integration grants Snowflake outbound access to external endpoints: `enabled` gates whether it is live, `apiAllowedPrefixes` and `apiBlockedPrefixes` constrain which URLs calls may reach, and `apiAwsRoleArn`, `apiAwsExternalId`, `azureTenantId`, and `azureAdApplicationId` expose the assumed role and tenant trust. The `properties` map returns the complete DESCRIBE API INTEGRATION output for any field not surfaced individually.

application.name: application
application.title: Snowflake Native App
application.desc: An installed Snowflake Native App in the account, keyed by name. Native Apps run provider-supplied code inside the consumer account with granted privileges, so they are the account's third-party-code and supply-chain surface. Covers where the app was installed from (a Marketplace listing or a local application package), the installed version and patch, and the owning role. Select an app by name, for example `snowflake.applications.where(name == "SECURITY_APP")`.

applicationPackage.name: applicationPackage
applicationPackage.title: Snowflake application package
applicationPackage.desc: An application package in the account, keyed by name. Application packages are the provider side of Snowflake Native Apps, bundling the code and data that become an installed application. Covers the release distribution (internal or external), the application class, and the owning role. Select a package by name, for example `snowflake.applicationPackages.where(name == "MY_APP_PKG")`.

applicationRole.name: applicationRole
applicationRole.title: Snowflake application role
applicationRole.desc: Role defined by an installed Snowflake Native App, keyed by name, which the app uses to grant consumers access to the objects it creates. Application roles live inside the app rather than in the account role hierarchy, so they are the record of what an installed app exposes to whoever it is shared with. Select a role by name, for example `snowflake.account.applications.first.roles.where(name == "APP_PUBLIC")`.

asset.name: asset
asset.title: Asset this root belongs to
asset.desc: Platform, version, identity and labels of the asset this root describes.

authenticationPolicy.name: authenticationPolicy
authenticationPolicy.title: Snowflake Authentication Policy
authenticationPolicy.desc: Authentication policy governing which login methods, MFA requirements, and client types are permitted for the account or the users it is attached to. This is the definitive control for whether MFA is enforced and whether password authentication is still allowed, so it is central to auditing login security. The `authenticationMethods` and `mfaAuthenticationMethods` fields report the permitted method sets, `mfaEnrollment` reports whether MFA is REQUIRED or OPTIONAL, `clientTypes` restricts which client applications may connect, and `securityIntegrations` lists the external auth integrations the policy allows.

connection.name: connection
connection.title: Snowflake Connection
connection.desc: Account-level connection object used for Business Critical failover and client redirect across replicated accounts, exposing a stable connection URL that clients target while the underlying primary account can change. Auditing connections surfaces which account currently serves as primary (`isPrimary`, `primary`), the accounts failover is permitted to (`failoverAllowedToAccounts`), and the durable `connectionUrl` clients use. Connections are selected by `name`.

cortexSearchService.name: cortexSearchService
cortexSearchService.title: Snowflake Cortex Search service
cortexSearchService.desc: A Cortex Search service in the account, the managed retrieval index that powers low-latency semantic and keyword search over a source query's text, the retrieval half of a Cortex retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) application. Covers where the service lives (databaseName, schemaName, name), the warehouse that runs indexing and query serving, the target data freshness lag, the query that defines the indexed source data, and the URL clients call to issue searches. The query definition and service URL are high-value review targets: together they reveal exactly which data a service exposes and where it can be reached. Select a service by name, for example `snowflake.account.cortexSearchServices.where(name == "SUPPORT_DOCS")`.

database.name: database
database.title: Snowflake Database
database.desc: Logical container that holds schemas, tables, views, and other objects in a Snowflake account. Auditing databases surfaces ownership, Time Travel data retention, transient (non-fail-safe) status, and the database-scoped roles that grant access to its contents. The `origin` field identifies a database created from a share or replica, and `roles` enumerates the roles defined within the database. The database-scoped data-governance controls are reachable through `schemas`, `maskingPolicies`, `rowAccessPolicies`, `tags`, and `secrets`, mirroring the account-wide collections but limited to this database. Asset discovery emits each database as its own asset, so these fields also form the posture surface scanned per database.

databaseRole.name: databaseRole
databaseRole.title: Snowflake Database Role
databaseRole.desc: Database-scoped role that grants privileges confined to a single database, used to model least-privilege access without account-wide reach. Audit these to see who owns each role (`owner` and `ownerRoleType`, where the owner is either a ROLE or a DATABASE_ROLE) and how roles nest into one another. The grant counts (`grantedToRoles`, `grantedToDatabaseRoles`, and `grantedDatabaseRoles`) reveal the depth of the role chain, which matters when reasoning about effective privilege escalation.

dynamicTable.name: dynamicTable
dynamicTable.title: Snowflake dynamic table
dynamicTable.desc: Dynamic table in a schema, keyed by name, a table whose contents Snowflake refreshes from a defining query on a declared freshness target. A dynamic table runs its query on a warehouse without a task or a schedule of its own, which makes it an automation surface that reads whatever the defining query reaches. The `text` field holds that query. Covers the warehouse the refresh runs on, the target lag that sets how stale the data may become, the refresh mode Snowflake chose and why, the scheduling state, and whether the table is a clone or a replica. Select a dynamic table by name, for example `snowflake.account.dynamicTables.where(schedulingState == "ACTIVE")`.

eventTable.name: eventTable
eventTable.title: Snowflake event table
eventTable.desc: Event table in a schema, keyed by name, the destination Snowflake writes log entries, trace spans, and other telemetry to from functions, procedures, and stored code. An event table receives whatever the emitting code logs, which can include argument values and other sensitive data, so its ownership governs who can read that record. Select an event table by name, for example `snowflake.account.eventTables.where(name == "TELEMETRY_EVENTS")`.

externalAccessIntegration.name: externalAccessIntegration
externalAccessIntegration.title: Snowflake external access integration
externalAccessIntegration.desc: An external access integration in the account, keyed by name. External access integrations are the account's outbound-egress control: they whitelist which network rules (hostnames and ports), secrets, and API authentication integrations a function or procedure may reach, so they are central to preventing data exfiltration from user code. Covers whether the integration is enabled and the allowed network rules, secrets, and API authentication integrations. Select an integration by name, for example `snowflake.externalAccessIntegrations.where(enabled == true)`.

externalTable.name: externalTable
externalTable.title: Snowflake external table
externalTable.desc: External table in a schema, keyed by name, a table whose data stays in cloud object storage instead of Snowflake. External tables read across the account boundary, so the storage location, the stage that reaches it, and the cloud and region that hold it are the review targets: together they show exactly which outside storage the account reads. Covers the backing stage and location, the file format the data is parsed with, the notification channel that drives automatic refresh, refresh state, and whether Snowflake considers the table invalid. Select an external table by name, for example `snowflake.account.externalTables.where(name == "RAW_EVENTS")`.

externalVolume.name: externalVolume
externalVolume.title: Snowflake external volume
externalVolume.desc: External volume in the account, keyed by name, the named external storage that backs Iceberg tables. An external volume holds account data outside Snowflake and names the cloud credentials used to reach it, so the storage locations are the trust boundary: each one records the cloud provider, the base URL, and the role or service account Snowflake assumes to read and write there. `allowWrites` reports whether Snowflake may write to that storage at all. Select a volume by name, for example `snowflake.account.externalVolumes.where(allowWrites == true)`.

failoverGroup.name: failoverGroup
failoverGroup.title: Snowflake Failover Group
failoverGroup.desc: Failover or replication group that copies account-level objects to secondary accounts for disaster recovery and business continuity. The `type` field distinguishes a failover group (ACCOUNT) from a replication group (BUSINESS_CONTINUITY), and `isPrimary` marks whether this account holds the source group or a read-only replica. Auditing these groups confirms that critical databases and shares are replicated to the intended target accounts and, via `replicationSchedule` and `secondaryState`, that replicas are refreshing on the expected cadence rather than drifting or sitting suspended.

fileFormat.name: fileFormat
fileFormat.title: Snowflake file format
fileFormat.desc: File format in a schema, keyed by name, the named set of parsing rules Snowflake applies when it reads staged data files. A file format decides how staged bytes become rows, so its options govern whether malformed input is rejected or silently coerced: settings such as error-on-column-count-mismatch and replace-invalid-characters determine whether a load fails loudly or quietly admits corrupted data. Covers the format type and the full option set for that type. Select a file format by name, for example `snowflake.account.fileFormats.where(type == "CSV")`.

function.name: function
function.title: Snowflake user-defined function
function.desc: A user-defined function (UDF) in a schema, keyed by name. UDFs run custom logic (SQL, JavaScript, Python, Java, or Scala) with the caller's or owner's rights, and can reach outside Snowflake through external access integrations and secrets, so they are a code-execution and data-egress surface. Covers the implementation language, whether the function is secure (its definition is hidden), whether it is an external function that calls an HTTP endpoint, the argument signature, and the bound external access integrations and secrets. Select a function by name, for example `snowflake.functions.where(language == "PYTHON")`.

grant.name: grant
grant.title: Snowflake Grant
grant.desc: Single privilege granted on a Snowflake object to a role, user, or share, as returned by SHOW GRANTS. Grants are the core of Snowflake access control, so auditing them reveals who holds which privileges on which objects and whether a grantee can re-grant them. The `grantedTo` field discriminates the grantee kind (ROLE, USER, SHARE, or DATABASE_ROLE), `grantedOn` identifies the object type (such as DATABASE or TABLE), and `grantOption` flags whether the grantee holds WITH GRANT OPTION.

managedAccount.name: managedAccount
managedAccount.title: Snowflake Managed Account
managedAccount.desc: Reader account provisioned by a provider account to share data with a consumer who has no Snowflake account of their own. Auditing managed accounts surfaces every reader account created for data sharing, where it lives (`cloud`, `region`), how it is reached (`url`, `accountLocatorUrl`, `locator`), and whether it is a reader account (`isReader`). Accounts are selected by `name`.

maskingPolicy.name: maskingPolicy
maskingPolicy.title: Snowflake Masking Policy
maskingPolicy.desc: Snowflake masking policy that redacts or transforms column values at query time based on the executing role or context. Auditing these policies reveals where sensitive data is protected and how: `body` holds the SQL CASE expression that implements the masking, `signature` gives the input columns and types the policy operates on (each as a `name:type` pair like `val:STRING`), and `references` enumerates every table, view, or column the policy is currently attached to. Policies are schema-scoped and selected by `name`, `databaseName`, and `schemaName`.

materializedView.name: materializedView
materializedView.title: Snowflake materialized view
materializedView.desc: Materialized view in a schema, keyed by name, a stored query whose results Snowflake persists and keeps current against a single source table. A materialized view copies data out of its source table into a separately governed object, so it can widen access to data the source table restricts. The `text` field holds the defining SQL, which shows exactly which columns and rows the view surfaces, and `isSecure` reports whether the definition is hidden from roles without access to the view. Covers the source table, the stored footprint in rows and bytes, refresh currency, and whether Snowflake considers the view invalid. Select a materialized view by name, for example `snowflake.account.materializedViews.where(isSecure == false)`.

networkPolicy.name: networkPolicy
networkPolicy.title: Snowflake Network Policy
networkPolicy.desc: Access control rule that restricts inbound access to the account, or to individual users, by source IP address and network rule. Audit network policies to confirm that access is limited to trusted ranges: allowed and blocked IP addresses are exposed through `allowedIpList` and `blockedIpList`, and the referenced network rules through `allowedNetworkRules` and `blockedNetworkRules`, while the corresponding `entriesIn*` counts give the size of each list at a glance. The `name` field selects the policy, for example `snowflake.networkPolicy(name: "corp_ip_allowlist")`.

networkRule.name: networkRule
networkRule.title: Snowflake Network Rule
networkRule.desc: Named set of network identifiers (IP ranges, cloud private-link endpoints, or host:port pairs) that network policies and external-access integrations reference to allow or block traffic. The `type` field reports which kind of identifier the rule holds (HOST_PORT, AWSVPCEID, or AZURELINKID), and `mode` reports the traffic direction it governs (INGRESS, EGRESS, or INTERNAL_STAGE). The `valueList` field returns the actual identifiers, and `entriesInValueList` gives their count. Rules are schema-scoped and selected by `name`, `databaseName`, and `schemaName`.

notificationIntegration.name: notificationIntegration
notificationIntegration.title: Snowflake Notification Integration
notificationIntegration.desc: Account-level object that connects Snowflake to an external messaging or queue service (Amazon SNS/SQS, Google Pub/Sub, or Azure Event Grid) for event notifications and auto-ingest pipelines. Auditing notification integrations surfaces the trust edge to external messaging: `enabled` gates whether it is live, `direction` reports inbound versus outbound flow, `notificationProvider` names the backing service, and the provider-specific fields expose the topics, subscriptions, and roles involved. The `properties` map returns the complete DESCRIBE NOTIFICATION INTEGRATION output for any field not surfaced individually.

organizationAccount.name: organizationAccount
organizationAccount.title: Snowflake Organization Account
organizationAccount.desc: Account belonging to the same Snowflake organization as the account being scanned, as reported to a session holding ORGADMIN. Each entry carries the account name and locator, the region and edition it runs in, the URL clients connect to, and whether the account itself holds ORGADMIN through isOrgAdmin, which names the accounts that can create, drop, and move other accounts in the organization. Select an account by name, for example `snowflake.account.organizationAccounts.where(accountName == "PROD")`.

parameter.name: parameter
parameter.title: Snowflake Parameter
parameter.desc: Configuration parameter governing account, session, or object behavior, such as session timeouts, network policy binding, and data-governance defaults. Auditing parameters surfaces settings that weaken security posture when left at unsafe values. The `key` field selects the parameter by name, for example `snowflake.account.parameters.where(key == "STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS")`. The `level` field reports the scope at which the effective value was set, letting you distinguish an explicit override from an inherited default.

passwordPolicy.name: passwordPolicy
passwordPolicy.title: Snowflake Password Policy
passwordPolicy.desc: Password policy governing complexity and rotation rules for user passwords in the account, letting you audit whether length, character-class, age, reuse, and lockout requirements meet your baseline. Complexity controls surface as integers such as `passwordMinLength`, `passwordMinSpecialChars`, `passwordMaxAgeDays`, `passwordMaxRetries`, and `passwordHistory`. Password policies are scoped to a schema, so `databaseName` and `schemaName` identify where the policy lives.

pipe.name: pipe
pipe.title: Snowflake pipe
pipe.desc: Pipe in a schema, keyed by name, a continuous loader that copies files from a stage into a table as they arrive. A pipe runs its COPY statement without a caller, so the `definition` field is the authoritative record of which stage it reads and which table it writes, and the notification integration and channel show what triggers it from outside the account. Covers the load statement, the integrations that drive automatic ingestion and receive load errors, the file pattern the pipe matches, and why Snowflake considers a pipe invalid. Select a pipe by name, for example `snowflake.account.pipes.where(name == "INGEST_EVENTS")`.

policyReference.name: policyReference
policyReference.title: Snowflake Policy Reference
policyReference.desc: Single attachment of a governance policy (masking, row-access, password, projection, aggregation, or authentication) to a Snowflake entity, as reported by INFORMATION_SCHEMA.POLICY_REFERENCES. Each reference pairs the policy identity (policyDatabase, policySchema, policyName, policyKind) with the protected entity (refDatabaseName, refSchemaName, refEntityName, and refEntityDomain, one of ACCOUNT, INTEGRATION, TABLE, TAG, USER, or VIEW). refColumnName names the column for column-level masking, and tagName is populated when the policy is attached indirectly through a tag. Audit these to see where a policy is enforced across an account and whether each attachment is currently active (policyStatus).

procedure.name: procedure
procedure.title: Snowflake Procedure
procedure.desc: Stored procedure or built-in system procedure available in a Snowflake account. Procedures run custom logic with the caller's or owner's rights, so their definition and security posture matter for audits. The `isSecure` flag marks a procedure whose definition is hidden from users without ownership, and `isBuiltin` distinguishes account-defined procedures from Snowflake's system procedures.

resourceMonitor.name: resourceMonitor
resourceMonitor.title: Snowflake Resource Monitor
resourceMonitor.desc: Resource monitor that caps credit consumption for one or more warehouses, the primary control for preventing runaway compute spend. A monitor tracks credit usage against a quota and can trigger notifications or suspend warehouses once configured thresholds are crossed. The `level` field indicates whether the monitor applies at the ACCOUNT or WAREHOUSE scope. `notifyAt` lists the usage percentages that trigger notifications, while `suspendAt` and `suspendImmediateAt` give the percentages at which warehouses are suspended (null when not configured).

role.name: role
role.title: Snowflake Role
role.desc: Role in the account's access-control model, the unit that privileges are granted to and that users and other roles inherit. Auditing roles reveals who holds which privileges and how they chain through the role hierarchy, which is central to least-privilege review. The `owner` holds administrative control over the role, `grants` lists the privileges granted to the role (SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE), and `grantees` lists the users and roles the role has in turn been granted to (SHOW GRANTS OF ROLE). The `assignedToUsers`, `grantedToRoles`, and `grantedRoles` counts summarize the role's reach and its position in the hierarchy.

rowAccessPolicy.name: rowAccessPolicy
rowAccessPolicy.title: Snowflake Row-Access Policy
rowAccessPolicy.desc: Row-level access-control policy that filters which rows a query returns based on the executing role or context. Auditing row-access policies surfaces the columns each policy inspects (`signature` as `name:type` pairs), the SQL predicate it enforces (`body`), and every table or view it is attached to (`references`), so you can verify sensitive datasets are gated as intended. Policies are schema-scoped and selected by `name`, `databaseName`, and `schemaName`.

schema.name: schema
schema.title: Snowflake Schema
schema.desc: Logical container within a database that groups tables, views, and other objects and carries its own retention and ownership settings. Schemas are enumerated across every database in the account, each reporting its parent `databaseName`, and are selected by `name`. `retentionTime` gives the Time Travel data-retention window in days, `isDefault` and `isCurrent` mark the session's active schema, and `ownerRoleType` distinguishes a standard role owner from a database role.

secret.name: secret
secret.title: Snowflake Secret
secret.desc: Snowflake-managed secret that stores the credentials Snowflake objects use to authenticate to external systems, referenced by external functions, notification integrations, and similar objects. Auditing secrets surfaces what kind of credential is held (`secretType` is PASSWORD, OAUTH2, or GENERIC_STRING), which security or API integration a secret is bound to, and the expiry deadlines on OAuth access and refresh tokens, so stale or over-scoped credentials can be flagged. The `oauthScopes` field records the OAuth scopes granted to the secret, and ownership is captured by `owner` and `ownerRoleType`.

securityIntegration.name: securityIntegration
securityIntegration.title: Snowflake Security Integration
securityIntegration.desc: Security integration that configures how the account interoperates with external identity providers and authorization services, such as SAML2 single sign-on, OAuth clients, SCIM user provisioning, and external OAuth token validation. Auditing these integrations reveals which federation and delegated-authentication paths are trusted for account access, whether each is enabled, and how single sign-on is configured. The `type` field distinguishes the integration kind (for example SAML2 or OAUTH), and `properties` returns the full DESCRIBE SECURITY INTEGRATION result as a key/value map keyed by property name (SAML2_X509_CERT, SAML2_ISSUER, OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, and so on). The `saml2*` fields pull the corresponding single-sign-on settings out of that map for integrations of type SAML2.

sequence.name: sequence
sequence.title: Snowflake sequence
sequence.desc: Sequence in a schema, keyed by name, a generator of monotonically increasing numbers used for surrogate keys and similar identifiers. Covers the next value the sequence will hand out, the step between values, and whether values are guaranteed to be issued in order. Select a sequence by name, for example `snowflake.account.sequences.where(name == "ORDER_ID_SEQ")`.

sessionPolicy.name: sessionPolicy
sessionPolicy.title: Snowflake session policy
sessionPolicy.desc: Session policy that controls how long a session may remain idle before Snowflake terminates it, a lever for limiting the window in which an unattended or hijacked session stays usable. The `sessionIdleTimeoutMins` value (Snowflake default 240) applies to all session types, while `sessionUiIdleTimeoutMins` applies specifically to Snowsight browser sessions, so the two can enforce a tighter bound on interactive UI logins.

share.name: share
share.title: Snowflake Share
share.desc: Snowflake data share, the mechanism for exposing a database to other accounts. Auditing shares matters because they cross account boundaries: an OUTBOUND share grants external accounts read access to your data, so its `to` list is the set of accounts that can consume `databaseName`. The `kind` field distinguishes an OUTBOUND share (created by this account) from an INBOUND share (consumed from another account); for INBOUND shares `name` is fully qualified as account.share, and for OUTBOUND shares it is the bare share name.

stage.name: stage
stage.title: Snowflake Stage
stage.desc: Named location where Snowflake loads and unloads bulk data, either an internal stage backed by Snowflake-managed storage or an external stage pointing at a cloud bucket. The `type` field distinguishes INTERNAL from EXTERNAL, and for external stages `cloud`, `url`, `endpoint`, and `storeIntegration` describe the backing object store. Audit `hasCredentials` and `hasEncryptionKey` to find stages that embed inline credentials or a customer-supplied encryption key rather than relying on a storage integration, and `directoryEnabled` to see whether a directory table exposes file metadata over the staged contents.

storageIntegration.name: storageIntegration
storageIntegration.title: Snowflake Storage Integration
storageIntegration.desc: Account-level object that grants Snowflake access to external cloud storage (Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob) without exposing static credentials, referenced by external stages. Auditing storage integrations matters because they define a trust boundary to external buckets: `enabled` gates whether it is live, `storageAllowedLocations` and `storageBlockedLocations` constrain which URLs stages may reach, and the provider-specific fields (`storageAwsRoleArn`, `storageAwsIamUserArn`, `storageGcpServiceAccount`, `azureTenantId`, `azureConsentUrl`) expose the assumed identity on each cloud. The `properties` map returns the complete DESCRIBE STORAGE INTEGRATION output for any field not surfaced individually.

stream.name: stream
stream.title: Snowflake stream
stream.desc: Stream in a schema, keyed by name, a change-data-capture reader that records the rows inserted, updated, and deleted in a source table since the stream was last consumed. A stream reads whatever its source table holds, so it carries that data forward into whatever consumes the stream, which makes the source table and base tables the review targets. Covers the source object and the base tables behind it, the kind of change data recorded, and staleness: a stream that goes stale silently stops delivering change data, so `stale` and `staleAfter` show whether the pipeline reading it has quietly stopped. Select a stream by name, for example `snowflake.account.streams.where(stale == true)`.

streamlit.name: streamlit
streamlit.title: Snowflake Streamlit app
streamlit.desc: Streamlit app in a schema, keyed by name, a Python data application Snowflake hosts and serves to users through a generated URL. A Streamlit app runs queries against the account on behalf of whoever opens it, so the serving URL and the warehouse it runs queries on describe its reach. Select an app by name, for example `snowflake.account.streamlits.where(name == "SALES_APP")`.

table.name: table
table.title: Snowflake table
table.desc: Table in a schema, keyed by name, the primary store for account data and so the main subject of data-protection review. Covers the physical footprint in rows and bytes, the time-travel retention window that governs how long deleted or changed data stays recoverable, whether change tracking records row-level history for streams, whether search optimization has built an access path over the data, and whether the table is backed by external storage or collects telemetry as an event table. Select a table by name, for example `snowflake.account.tables.where(name == "CUSTOMERS")`.

tag.name: tag
tag.title: Snowflake Tag
tag.desc: Schema-level label used for governance, data classification, and policy attachment across Snowflake objects. A tag is identified by `name` within its `databaseName` and `schemaName`. When `allowedValues` is non-empty, the tag is constrained to that set of permitted string values, letting you audit whether sensitive-data tagging follows an approved vocabulary; an empty list means the tag accepts any value. `ownerRoleType` distinguishes a standard role owner from a database role.

task.name: task
task.title: Snowflake task
task.desc: A scheduled or triggered unit of SQL in a schema, keyed by name. Tasks run with the owner's rights on a warehouse and a schedule, which makes them a common automation surface and a persistence or privilege-escalation vector. Covers the warehouse the task runs on, the schedule and predecessor relationships that form a task graph, the run state, the SQL definition and its gating condition, and whether overlapping runs are allowed. Select a task by name, for example `snowflake.tasks.where(name == "REFRESH_SALES")`.

user.name: user
user.title: Snowflake User
user.desc: Snowflake user account, covering login identity, authentication state (password, RSA key-pair, and Duo external authentication), access controls (disabled status, forced password change, default role and default warehouse), and lifecycle timestamps. Auditing users surfaces dormant or stale accounts, missing credential hygiene, and over-broad default roles. `daysSinceLastLogin` is derived from the last successful login and returns -1 when the user has never logged in. `grants` lists the roles granted directly to this user, and `parameters` lists user-level parameter overrides.

view.name: view
view.title: Snowflake View
view.desc: View or materialized view defined in a Snowflake schema, exposing a stored query over one or more underlying tables. The `text` field holds the view definition SQL, which reveals exactly what data the view surfaces, and `isSecure` reports whether it is a secure view that hides its definition and restricts what unauthorized roles can read. Materialized views (`isMaterialized`) persist query results for faster reads. Query views to review data exposure, ownership, and the SQL behind derived datasets.

warehouse.name: warehouse
warehouse.title: Snowflake Warehouse
warehouse.desc: Snowflake virtual warehouse that provides the compute resources for query execution and data loading. Warehouse size, multi-cluster counts, and auto-suspend behavior drive both credit consumption and performance, so these records support audits of idle-timeout hygiene, cluster scaling limits, and credit governance through the associated resource monitor. Live utilization is reported in available, provisioning, quiescing, and other, while running and queued reflect the current query load.

snowflake.title: Snowflake Data Cloud
snowflake.desc: Root namespace for all Snowflake resources. Query `snowflake.account` for users, roles, security integrations, password and network policies, warehouses, databases, stages, shares, API integrations, tags, failover groups, and grants. `currentRole` returns the role active for the current session.

accountAdmins.name: accountAdmins
accountAdmins.title: Users that hold the ACCOUNTADMIN role (directly or indirectly via role grants)

alerts.name: alerts
alerts.title: Alerts in the account (scheduled condition checks that run an action)

applicationPackages.name: applicationPackages
applicationPackages.title: Application packages in the account (Native App providers)

snowflake.alert.title: Snowflake alert
snowflake.alert.desc: Alert in a schema, keyed by name, a scheduled check that evaluates a SQL condition and runs a SQL action whenever the condition returns rows. An alert runs on a schedule with the owner's rights and no caller, so `condition` and `action` together are the record of what it reads and what it does, which makes it both a monitoring control and an automation surface worth reviewing. A suspended alert stops running silently, so `state` shows whether a control that is configured is actually operating. Select an alert by name, for example `snowflake.account.alerts.where(state == "suspended")`.

properties.title: DESCRIBE API INTEGRATION output

Common keys are API_AWS_ROLE_ARN, API_AWS_EXTERNAL_ID, API_ALLOWED_PREFIXES, API_BLOCKED_PREFIXES, AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_AD_APPLICATION_ID, ENABLED, and COMMENT. The set of keys depends on `type`, so AWS keys are absent on an Azure integration and vice versa. Prefix and credential values are also available individually via apiAllowedPrefixes, apiAwsRoleArn, and the other dedicated fields.

snowflake.apiIntegration.title: Snowflake API Integration
snowflake.apiIntegration.desc: API integration object holding the cloud authentication context that external functions and Git repository integrations use to reach an HTTPS proxy service. The `type` field selects the backing provider (aws_api_gateway, azure_api_management, or google_api_gateway) and determines which credential fields carry a value. Auditing these matters because the integration grants Snowflake outbound access to external endpoints: `enabled` gates whether it is live, `apiAllowedPrefixes` and `apiBlockedPrefixes` constrain which URLs calls may reach, and `apiAwsRoleArn`, `apiAwsExternalId`, `azureTenantId`, and `azureAdApplicationId` expose the assumed role and tenant trust. The `properties` map returns the complete DESCRIBE API INTEGRATION output for any field not surfaced individually.

patPolicy.title: Programmatic access token rules
patPolicy.desc: The PAT_POLICY value from DESCRIBE AUTHENTICATION POLICY, as a map keyed by sub-parameter name. DEFAULT_EXPIRY_IN_DAYS and MAX_EXPIRY_IN_DAYS are numbers; NETWORK_POLICY_EVALUATION is ENFORCED_REQUIRED, ENFORCED_NOT_REQUIRED or NOT_ENFORCED; REQUIRE_ROLE_RESTRICTION_FOR_SERVICE_USERS and REQUIRE_ROLE_RESTRICTION_FOR_PERSON_USERS are booleans; BLOCKED_ROLES_LIST is a list of role names a token may never assume. Together these decide whether a programmatic access token is bounded in lifetime, whether it is usable from any network, and what it may act as, for example `patPolicy["NETWORK_POLICY_EVALUATION"] == "ENFORCED_REQUIRED"` or `patPolicy["MAX_EXPIRY_IN_DAYS"] <= 90`. These decide which external identities may federate into the account at all. Every value is a list of strings, so an account id keeps its leading zeros. A sub-parameter that places no restriction reports the single member ALL rather than an empty list, so an unrestricted policy reads as `workloadIdentityPolicy["ALLOWED_PROVIDERS"].contains("ALL")`. snowflake.authenticationPolicy.title: Snowflake Authentication Policy

This is the definitive control for whether MFA is enforced and whether password authentication is still allowed, so it is central to auditing login security. The `authenticationMethods` and `mfaAuthenticationMethods` fields report the permitted method sets, `mfaEnrollment` reports whether MFA is REQUIRED or OPTIONAL, `clientTypes` restricts which client applications may connect, and `securityIntegrations` lists the external auth integrations the policy allows.

snowflake.database.title: Snowflake Database
snowflake.database.desc: Logical container that holds schemas, tables, views, and other objects in a Snowflake account. Auditing databases surfaces ownership, Time Travel data retention, transient (non-fail-safe) status, and the database-scoped roles that grant access to its contents. The `origin` field identifies a database created from a share or replica, and `roles` enumerates the roles defined within the database. The database-scoped data-governance controls are reachable through `schemas`, `maskingPolicies`, `rowAccessPolicies`, `tags`, and `secrets`, mirroring the account-wide collections but limited to this database. Asset discovery emits each database as its own asset, so these fields also form the posture surface scanned per database.

snowflake.table.title: Snowflake table
snowflake.table.desc: Table in a schema, keyed by name, the primary store for account data and so the main subject of data-protection review. Covers the physical footprint in rows and bytes, the time-travel retention window that governs how long deleted or changed data stays recoverable, whether change tracking records row-level history for streams, whether search optimization has built an access path over the data, and whether the table is backed by external storage or collects telemetry as an event table. Select a table by name, for example `snowflake.account.tables.where(name == "CUSTOMERS")`.

snowflake.tag.title: Snowflake Tag
snowflake.tag.desc: Schema-level label used for governance, data classification, and policy attachment across Snowflake objects. A tag is identified by `name` within its `databaseName` and `schemaName`. When `allowedValues` is non-empty, the tag is constrained to that set of permitted string values, letting you audit whether sensitive-data tagging follows an approved vocabulary; an empty list means the tag accepts any value. `ownerRoleType` distinguishes a standard role owner from a database role.

snowflake.task.title: Snowflake task
snowflake.task.desc: A scheduled or triggered unit of SQL in a schema, keyed by name. Tasks run with the owner's rights on a warehouse and a schedule, which makes them a common automation surface and a persistence or privilege-escalation vector. Covers the warehouse the task runs on, the schedule and predecessor relationships that form a task graph, the run state, the SQL definition and its gating condition, and whether overlapping runs are allowed. Select a task by name, for example `snowflake.tasks.where(name == "REFRESH_SALES")`.

snowflake.user.name: snowflake.user

authenticationPolicy.name: authenticationPolicy
authenticationPolicy.title: Authentication policy attached to the user
authenticationPolicy.desc: The policy that decides which authentication methods and client types the user may sign in with, and whether a second factor is required. Null when no policy is attached to the user directly, in which case the account policy applies.

daysSinceLastLogin.name: daysSinceLastLogin
daysSinceLastLogin.title: Number of days since the user last successfully logged in (-1 if never logged in)

defaultNamespace.name: defaultNamespace
defaultNamespace.title: Namespace that is active by default

defaultSecondaryRoles.name: defaultSecondaryRoles
defaultSecondaryRoles.title: Secondary roles activated by default in a session
defaultSecondaryRoles.desc: Contains ALL when the user automatically activates every role granted to them, which broadens the privileges available in a session beyond the primary role. Empty when no secondary roles activate by default.

defaultWarehouseRef.name: defaultWarehouseRef
defaultWarehouseRef.title: Virtual warehouse that is active by default for the user

effectiveGrants.name: effectiveGrants
effectiveGrants.title: All privileges the user holds through their roles
effectiveGrants.desc: The union of the grants held by every role in effectiveRoles, deduplicated. Privileges never attach to a user directly, so this is the user's real authorization surface.

effectiveRoles.name: effectiveRoles
effectiveRoles.title: All roles the user holds, directly or through role grants
effectiveRoles.desc: The direct roles plus every role those roles inherit, so a user who reaches ACCOUNTADMIN only through an intermediate custom role still reports it.

extAuthnDuo.name: extAuthnDuo
extAuthnDuo.title: Whether the user is enrolled in Duo MFA via Snowflake's external authenticator

extAuthnUid.name: extAuthnUid
extAuthnUid.title: Duo external-authentication user ID linking the Snowflake user to their Duo account

grants.name: grants
grants.title: Roles granted directly to this user (SHOW GRANTS TO USER)
grants.desc: Each entry names a role in `name`, with `grantedOn` set to ROLE. Snowflake reports no privilege for this statement, so `privilege` is null; `grantOption` is false, because a role grant carries no grant option and a user can never re-grant a role they hold. Prefer roles, which resolves the same rows to role resources.

hasMfa.name: hasMfa
hasMfa.title: Whether the user has multi-factor authentication enrolled

hasPassword.name: hasPassword
hasPassword.title: Whether the user has a password

hasRsaPublicKey.name: hasRsaPublicKey
hasRsaPublicKey.title: Whether the user has an RSA public key registered for key-pair authentication

lastSuccessLogin.name: lastSuccessLogin
lastSuccessLogin.title: Last time the user logged in

lockedUntil.name: lockedUntil
lockedUntil.title: Time until the user is locked

minsToBypassMfa.name: minsToBypassMfa
minsToBypassMfa.title: Minutes remaining in a temporary MFA bypass window
minsToBypassMfa.desc: Non-empty while an administrator has temporarily allowed the user to sign in without MFA. Empty when no bypass window is active.

mustChangePassword.name: mustChangePassword
mustChangePassword.title: Whether the user is forced to change their password

networkPolicy.name: networkPolicy
networkPolicy.title: Network policy applied to the user
networkPolicy.desc: Null when the user has no per-user override, and also when the named policy cannot be listed by the scanning role, in which case networkPolicyName still reports that an override is set.

networkPolicyName.name: networkPolicyName
networkPolicyName.title: Name of the network policy applied to the user
networkPolicyName.desc: A per-user network policy replaces the account-level policy, so a user carrying one is not restricted by the account's allowed IP ranges. Empty when the user has no override and inherits the account policy.

passwordPolicy.name: passwordPolicy
passwordPolicy.title: Password policy attached to the user
passwordPolicy.desc: Null when no policy is attached to the user directly, in which case the account policy applies.

roles.name: roles
roles.title: Roles granted to the user directly
roles.desc: Snowflake grants privileges to roles rather than to users, so these are the entry points into everything the user can do. Use effectiveRoles for the roles reached through them.

rsaPublicKey2SetAt.name: rsaPublicKey2SetAt
rsaPublicKey2SetAt.title: When the secondary key-pair public key was last set
rsaPublicKey2SetAt.desc: The time the most recent statement assigning RSA_PUBLIC_KEY_2 to this user succeeded. The second slot exists so a new key can be staged before the old one is retired, so during a rotation both this and rsaPublicKeySetAt carry a value. Null when the second slot has never been used, and subject to the same one-year history window as rsaPublicKeySetAt.

rsaPublicKeySetAt.name: rsaPublicKeySetAt
rsaPublicKeySetAt.title: When the primary key-pair public key was last set
rsaPublicKeySetAt.desc: The time the most recent statement assigning RSA_PUBLIC_KEY to this user succeeded, for assessing how long a key-pair credential has gone without rotation, for example `snowflake.account.users.where(hasRsaPublicKey).all(rsaPublicKeySetAt > time.now - 90*time.day)`. Snowflake records no set time on the user itself, so this is correlated from the account query history, which is retained for one year: a key last set before that window, or on an account where the history cannot be read, reports null rather than a date.

sessionPolicy.name: sessionPolicy
sessionPolicy.title: Session policy attached to the user
sessionPolicy.desc: Null when no policy is attached to the user directly, in which case the account policy applies.

snowflakeLock.name: snowflakeLock
snowflakeLock.title: Whether Snowflake has temporarily locked the user after repeated failed sign-in attempts

type.name: type
type.title: User type
type.desc: One of PERSON, SERVICE, or LEGACY_SERVICE. SERVICE and LEGACY_SERVICE users cannot sign in with a password or MFA and authenticate with a key pair or OAuth, so this field separates human users from machine identities during access review.

snowflake.user.title: Snowflake User
snowflake.user.desc: Snowflake user account, covering login identity, authentication state (password, RSA key-pair, and Duo external authentication), access controls (disabled status, forced password change, default role and default warehouse), and lifecycle timestamps. Auditing users surfaces dormant or stale accounts, missing credential hygiene, and over-broad default roles. `daysSinceLastLogin` is derived from the last successful login and returns -1 when the user has never logged in. `grants` lists the roles granted directly to this user, and `parameters` lists user-level parameter overrides.

databaseName.name: databaseName
databaseName.title: Database name

ownerRoleType.name: ownerRoleType
ownerRoleType.title: Type of the role that owns the resource (ROLE or DATABASE_ROLE)

reserved.name: reserved
reserved.title: Reserved flag set by Snowflake (typically empty; reserved for future use)

schemaName.name: schemaName
schemaName.title: Schema name

snowflake.view.title: Snowflake View
snowflake.view.desc: View or materialized view defined in a Snowflake schema, exposing a stored query over one or more underlying tables. The `text` field holds the view definition SQL, which reveals exactly what data the view surfaces, and `isSecure` reports whether it is a secure view that hides its definition and restricts what unauthorized roles can read. Materialized views (`isMaterialized`) persist query results for faster reads. Query views to review data exposure, ownership, and the SQL behind derived datasets.

snowflake.warehouse.name: snowflake.warehouse

autoResume.name: autoResume
autoResume.title: Whether the warehouse, if suspended, automatically resumes

autoSuspend.name: autoSuspend
autoSuspend.title: Period of inactivity, in seconds, after which a running warehouse automatically suspends and stops using credits

available.name: available

isCurrent.name: isCurrent
isCurrent.title: Whether the warehouse is a current warehouse

isDefault.name: isDefault
isDefault.title: Whether the warehouse is a default warehouse

other.name: other
other.title: Percentage of the warehouse compute not in available, provisioning, or quiescing state

ownerRoleType.name: ownerRoleType
ownerRoleType.title: Type of the role that owns the resource (ROLE or DATABASE_ROLE)

provisioning.name: provisioning
provisioning.title: Percentage of the warehouse compute resources in provisioning

quiescing.name: quiescing
quiescing.title: Percentage of the warehouse compute resources that execute queries

resourceMonitorRef.name: resourceMonitorRef
resourceMonitorRef.title: Resource monitor governing the warehouse's credit usage

scalingPolicy.name: scalingPolicy
scalingPolicy.title: Scaling policy
scalingPolicy.desc: Governs how a multi-cluster warehouse starts additional clusters under load, either STANDARD or ECONOMY.

size.name: size
size.title: Warehouse size
size.desc: Compute size, one of XSMALL, SMALL, MEDIUM, LARGE, XLARGE, XXLARGE, XXXLARGE, X4LARGE, X5LARGE, or X6LARGE.

state.name: state
state.title: Operational state
state.desc: One of STARTED, SUSPENDED, SUSPENDING, RESUMING, or RESIZING.

snowflake.warehouse.title: Snowflake Warehouse
snowflake.warehouse.desc: Snowflake virtual warehouse that provides the compute resources for query execution and data loading. Warehouse size, multi-cluster counts, and auto-suspend behavior drive both credit consumption and performance, so these records support audits of idle-timeout hygiene, cluster scaling limits, and credit governance through the associated resource monitor. Live utilization is reported in available, provisioning, quiescing, and other, while running and queued reflect the current query load.
